en: The First Fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-Paramaśrīmañjuśrīmūla-jñāna-paramarahasya-sarvārtha-nāmasamādhi*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven,
Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
At that time, the Great Mañjuśrī, the most excellent Vajrapāṇi,
who possesses all virtues, who is able to subdue those difficult to subdue,
the most supreme within the three realms, the most honored and great fearless one.
Within all the Secret Sections, he is the sovereign lord;
with the lotus eyes of perfect wisdom, his eyebrows are like a lotus.
Before the Buddha, the World-Honored One, he playfully hurls the vajra.
Again, in a mere instant, there appeared an infinite number of vajras surrounding him; as he playfully cast these vajras,
there were tens of millions of beings, radiant with vajra-light.
His face displays a frowning expression; he is courageous, great, and fearless, with majestic virtue that is exceptionally sublime.
He subdues all beings, possessing compassion, wisdom, and skillful means, benefiting both himself and the world.
Body and mind filled with great joy, attaining the most supreme and wondrous bliss;
again manifesting a wrathful form, all that the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
performs is fully embraced, universally obtaining benefit and happiness.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi prostrated to the Honored One of Perfect Enlightenment,
Śākyamuni Buddha, and with palms joined, addressed him, saying:
"All classes of sentient beings are foolishly submerged in the mire of birth and death."
Arising from afflictions and doubts, there is no means by which one can attain liberation;
I pray that you, out of compassion, may bring benefit and happiness to me and all sentient beings,
so that we may realize the truth as it is and fully understand the web of illusion.
The Buddha is the Teacher of the world; may he proclaim the true Dharma for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings, so that they may attain the unsurpassed fruit—
the great samādhi and the supreme, authentic wisdom of all Buddhas.
The World-Honored One’s assembly of perfect wisdom, which can discern the faculties, desires, and natures of sentient beings; the sublime virtue of the *uṣṇīṣa*,
the true wisdom, and the supreme self-arisen wisdom.
Thoroughly realizing the profound meaning, The all-encompassing, vast, peerless,
and tranquil meaning, The supreme and most excellent meaning—
Within this Great Yoga Tantra, These are the secret names and meanings.

The Section on the Noble Samādhi: Excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, it was taught by the Buddhas of the past, will be taught by the Buddhas of the future, and is now being taught by the World-Honored One of the present;
throughout the three times, it has been fully proclaimed.
Now, from this net of illusory transformations, I have been born;
with joy I grasp the great vajra and skillfully uphold all vidyās,
just as I have attained the Dharma, cherishing and maintaining it.
O You of most excellent and firm resolve, who abide in the secret mind of the Buddha according to the inclinations of sentient beings,
we pray that you will proclaim the supreme Dharma that extinguishes afflictions without remainder, so that the most excellent wisdom may be attained.
Thus, O Lord of Secrets, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi joined his palms in reverence, stood before him, and made this request.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, the Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings—
From the tongue and the gateway of the face, vast radiance issues forth,
universally illuminating the ten directions; it purifies all evil realms,
and wherever this light shines throughout the three worlds, the four māras are entirely subdued.
Again, he uttered a beautiful Brahma-voice that resounded throughout the three realms, praising the Lord of Secrets.
The Buddha of Great Power, Wisdom-Vajra-Time, spoke these words: "Excellent, O Vajradhara!"
O Auspicious and Most Supreme One, O Valiant Vajrapāṇi,
through your great compassion and skillful means, you have extensively benefited the world;
therefore, I entreat you to explain this secret dharma-gate.
This secret name and meaning— The supreme great auspiciousness of the fundamental wisdom of Samantabhadra, Which can subdue all māras and the like—
I shall now explain well; O Great Lord of Secrets!
Abiding in the supreme single-mindedness, listen attentively to what the Buddha has spoken.
At that time, Śākyamuni then proclaimed this Dharma,
which exhausts all mantra sections and the great vidyā-mantra section.
The Section on the Contemplation of the Three Mysteries; the Supreme Section of the Worldly and Transworldly;
the Supreme Section of the Great Seal (*Mahāmudrā*);
the Section of the *Uṣṇīṣa*; and all such sections as these.
Comprehensively encompassing all phenomena, these are the six great vidyārājas of secret name and meaning;
non-duality is spoken of as "duality," which is a phrase for the unarisen dharma, from which they are born.
This dharma abides within the mind of all wisdoms, as taught by all Buddhas of the three times.
Furthermore, the Great Mantra says:
The syllable A is right gnosis; from it, all Buddhas are born.
Furthermore, for the sake of all supreme signs, this is the meaning of the highest syllable, the great arising and non-arising.
Free from food, drink, and speech, one abandons the highest attachment; all vocal actions are purified.
Supremely predominant is greed, which stains the conduct of all sentient beings;
Supremely predominant is hatred, the great enemy among all afflictions;
Supremely predominant is delusion, which serves as an obstacle to wisdom for the ignorant and confused.
Supremely superior wrath, the great wrathful one, the great enemy;
supremely superior passion, entangled by all passions—
such as greed, hatred, and the rest— are all supremely superior.
The secret and wondrous Dharma-gate, Pervasive and capable of distancing one from grasping;
With the great sword of supreme wisdom, It shatters the crowns of all afflictions.
Manifesting a great color and a great body, Possessing great marks and great power.
Greatly renowned and of great majestic power, Greatly vast, perfect, of great desire, and great sovereignty;
Of great joy, great bliss, great love, and great fame;
Of great light, shining with great radiance.
Possessing all that is vast and great, Arising from great wisdom,
one thoroughly understands the great illusion; Accomplishing the meaning of the great illusion,
one attains the sublime bliss of the great illusion, And recognizes the fundamental net of illusion.
Great wealth and great donor, Upholder of the supreme pure precepts,
Great patience and great wisdom, Arouser of great diligence,
Great meditative concentration and equanimity, Mass of firm great intelligence.
Great skillful means and great vows, A great power and ocean of great wisdom;
The Dharma of great compassion and impartiality, With great mercy as the supreme increase,
Great insight that fully penetrates all, And great skillful means extensively enacted.
Possessing great supernormal powers and transformations, Great in conduct and exceedingly swift,
sovereign in great supernormal powers, Possessing great strength and great valor,
skillfully delivering all from the sufferings of existence, The Great Vajra Holder.
Greatly evil and extremely wrathful, he creates great terror that strikes fear into all;
the Great Radiance destroys all muteness. The Great Mantra, the most supreme Honored One, the Mahāyāna teaching that delivers and saves—the Mahāyāna, the most supreme teaching.
The Dharmakāya Mahāvairocana, the Greatly Quiescent, the Great Muni—
The wondrous Great Mantra, the Sovereign of the Great Mantra who has attained the ten pāramitās, relying upon those ten pāramitās.
The ten pāramitās are purified; the ten pāramitās are taught by the Sovereign of the Ten Stages.
Well-established in the ten stages, my ten knowledges are purified;
the ten knowledges are pure and firm.
The ten aspects and the ten meanings; the ten powers that pacify all faculties, the most supreme, true, and eternal meaning;
the ten aspects of ultimate tranquility, far removed from all conceptual proliferation; I and suchness are pure.
Your speech is true speech; your practice accords with the truth.
You speak without distinction or duality, yet you utter two words: all abide in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
With the lion’s roar of selflessness, you terrify those who cling to signs.
Liberated in all states, the Tathāgata with swift intent subdues all formidable enemies;
like a powerful wheel-turning monarch,
he is the supreme among all dharmas, the sovereign, and the object of veneration.
Of great majesty and great wisdom, unsurpassed by any teaching,
sovereign among all speech; you who possess boundless pure verbal activity and true words and meanings, proclaim the Four Noble Truths.
Following the assembly of śrāvakas— those non-retrogressive anāgāmins and arhats,
the venerable bhikṣus whose outflows are exhausted and who possess sharp faculties, as well as the courageous pratyekabuddhas.
Though arising in various forms, they share the same single true nature;
with the sword of wisdom, they sever all afflictions without remainder,
attaining peace and fearlessness, and abiding well within the limit of reality.
Having attained the perfection of knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, the Knower of the World,
for whom no marks of self can arise, abides in the Dharma of the two truths and has crossed to the further shore of saṃsāra; all that was to be done has been accomplished.
Born of pure, singular wisdom, with the sword of insight most fierce and sharp,
a mass of light of the True Dharma, illuminating both the mundane and supramundane worlds,
the Dharma King who possesses mastery over all phenomena proclaims the supreme path.
The meaning of the accomplishment of discernment, Free from all marks of conceptualization,
that realm of discernment is exhausted; It reveals the supreme dharmadhātu,
born of merit and the speech of merit, The great wisdom and the deeds of wisdom.
When one gives rise to the perception of right knowledge, two dharmas are born from this:
Ultimately free from all marks, they correspond to the mastery of meditative concentration,
immovable, and the supreme root of the three bodies.
Lord of the five bodies and correct wisdom, Great Sovereign of the five wisdoms,
exquisitely adorned with the crowns of the five Buddhas; pure with the five eyes and free from attachment,
most supreme among all Buddhas, you give birth to the sons of the Buddhas.
The supreme birth of wisdom, the single reality of the vajra produced within the True Dharma;
the supreme birth of the Lord of the World from space,
natural gnosis, the Great Wisdom, the Great Eye of Intelligence.
Great Radiance Pervading All, Great Wisdom-Light Great Sun, Wisdom-Light Illuminating the Lamp of the World;
Great Radiance Blazing, Supreme Mantra-Vidyārāja; Deeds of the Great King of Mantras.
Great Crown, True Crown, Sovereign Manifesting All Forms;
The Buddhas’ nature of selflessness universally illumines boundless realms.
Within it, all colors appear; I make offerings to the Great Sage.
Holding the vidyā-mantras of the three families, and the dhāraṇī-method of the Great Samaya;
holding the most supreme Three Jewels,
he proclaims the most excellent Three Vehicles and the supreme Amoghapāśa, the Vajrapāśa of great gathering.
The Vajra Hook and Great Lasso; the Great Vajra, the Terrifier,
and the Vajra Akṣobhya Buddha— these arise from the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom,
and from this wisdom are born all gates of skillful means.
He manifests in the form of great wrath; his appearance has six faces, six eyes, and six arms.
He is perfect and possesses great power, with sharp fangs protruding outward; he is exceedingly fierce and most terrifying.
Furthermore, he manifests the form of a great laugh, adorned with a hundred eyes;
he manifests as Yamāntaka, the terrifying Vajra-form,
the supreme Heart-Vajra, the vast Māyā-Vajra.
Supreme Vajra Family, incomparable Vajra-throne,
the immovable Ekajaṭī; adorned with elephant hide,
with the great malevolence of the sound "ha ha" and the great terror of the sound "hi hi."
The great laughter of the sound Aṭṭa; the great sound of Vajra-joy.
O Vajrasattva, Mahāsattva! O Vajrarāja, Great Bliss;
O Vajralakṣaṇa, Great Joy! The syllable HŪṂ is Vajra-wisdom.
Holding the vajra-knowledge arrow, wielding the vajra-sharp sword,
manifesting the vajra skillful activity; the vajra destroyer of enemy armies,
the vajra fire with its malevolent gaze, the blazing vajra-crest.
The Great Awakening of Vajra; the hundred-eyed Vajra illuminates the Vajra-jṛmbhas;
those comprised within a single jṛmbha number in the hundreds of millions (koṭi-nayuta); they abide in the Vajrasāra.
The Noble Vajradharamālā, adorned with vajra-jewels,
uttering the great sound of *hahaṭa*; with the hundred-syllable vajra-voice and wondrous resonance,
he roars a great cry that universally vibrates throughout the three realms.
The realm of space is boundless, and sound is likewise unimpeded;
Suchness is devoid of the mark of self, and the limit of reality is free from obstruction.
Emptiness transcends all speech; it is described as vast and profound.
He utters the sound of the great Dharma conch and strikes the great Dharma drum;
the Buddha’s majestic power is invincible. He beats the Dharma drum throughout the ten directions, manifesting form within the formless, with various forms most exquisite and wondrous.
Auspicious light of all colors, manifesting the supreme great lord of all remaining images;
great sovereign of the three realms, revealing the paths of all the noble ones;
you who raise the vast banner of the Dharma.
Within those three realms, he manifests in the form of a youth or appears with the features of an elder;
the Honored One, the Great Lord of the World,
is endowed with the thirty-two marks of perfection.
Pervading the three realms, you look upon them with joy;
With the merit of worldly wisdom, you act fearlessly in the world.
Supreme among the three realms, you are the sovereign and the refuge.
Born from the treasury of space, the ocean of the wisdom of all-knowledge,
Accumulated within the treasury of ignorance, he extinguishes all fetters of the three realms of existence;
With afflictions eliminated without remainder, he emerges and crosses to the shore beyond saṃsāra.
Wearing the crown of wisdom, consecrated by empowerment, adorned with perfect enlightenment,
he extinguishes the three types of suffering and the like; having attained liberation throughout the three times,
he is far removed from all obscurations, as pure as space.
The stains of affliction in the past are exactly the same throughout the three times;
all sentient beings, those great dragons, now manifest upon the peaks of mountains of merit,
having attained liberation like exquisite jewel lotuses.
That great wish-fulfilling gem, the most supreme among all jewels,
firm as a great kalpa-tree, and the greatest vessel of wisdom that benefits all sentient beings—
all these are produced through skillful means.
Pure wisdom and the wisdom of the pure factors, The samādhi-wisdom that most excellently discerns the faculties of sentient beings,
Possessing the wisdom of the threefold liberation,
the merit, and the dharma-wisdom— Vast benefit, great auspiciousness!
Auspicious, great, and most auspicious; Attaining renown, vast love, and the noble wealth of great riches;
Great joy and great bliss, virtuous in meaning and virtuous in action; Joyful renown and great auspiciousness.
The most supreme great vow, acting as the highest protection for all who face great terrors;
the Uṣṇīṣa of merit that causes all [fears] to be extinguished without remainder;
the most supreme and tranquil Uṣṇīṣa.
The Five-Eyed One with Five Topknots, the Lord of the Five-Cakras-Tufted Crown,
who possesses all great ascetic practices; he who holds his own view as liberation and practices according to his own realization— this is called the supreme brahmacarya.
They claim for themselves the status of Great Sages, asserting that they have already attained the ultimate Dharma;
they claim to be those who bathe their bodies like outsiders, and hold all views and such attachments to have arisen from Brahmā,
and that upon their cessation, they too shall be born in the realm of Brahmā.
Having attained liberation through disentanglement, one realizes the unimpeded and tranquil Dharma and attains peaceful Nirvāṇa; having attained the supreme Parinirvāṇa,
one reaches the limit of suffering and pleasure, and the phenomena of greed and the like are utterly extinguished.
"Unsurpassed and incomparable, signless and unattached—this is what is called the attained nirvana.
To hold such views as 'it transcends all paths' and so forth is a false attachment; these are all not the correct liberation."
They cannot comprehend that stainless seed, subtle, pure,
and free from the defilement of dust; it is utterly devoid of all faults,
realized only by perfect wisdom, and fully penetrated by the Omniscient One.
All those phenomena of consciousness are to be contemplated through non-dual wisdom,
free from doubt and conceptual discrimination; they share the same essence as the Buddhas of the three times,
having neither beginning nor end, and are perceived by the single eye of wisdom.
Born from the crown of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, identical in essence and stainless;
Sovereign of speech, great speech, supreme speech, and most excellent speech;
Unconquered lion’s roar, unsurpassed and peerless.
Universally manifesting the body of great joy, Or appearing in the form of a garland of fire,
or as auspicious and wondrous light; Great radiance, blazing and all-conquering sovereign,
The supreme state of the dharma free from defilement.
Like a supreme and wondrous medicine that subdues the enemies of all afflictions,
you are the great auspiciousness of the three realms. Establishing the maṇḍala of the multitude of stars,
you raise the great banner of the Dharma, its stupa-pole reaching throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
A single vast jeweled canopy pervades the entire world;
through the two dharmas of compassion, he forms the great maṇḍala of the Great Auspicious Lotus, adorned with sovereign mastery.
Adorned on all sides by supreme jewel canopies and the like,
The great sovereign of all Buddhas, The self-nature of the mind of all Buddhas,
The great correspondence of all Buddhas, The single teaching of all Buddhas.
Vajra-jewel empowerment, sovereign lord of all jewels,
King of all Avalokiteśvaras, and all Vajradharas,
The vast mind of all Buddhas, the supreme intention of all Buddhas.
The vast and expansive body of all Buddhas, the true speech of all Buddhas,
the Vajra Sun Great Illuminator; the vajra-pure root,
blazing with manifold colors, illuminating the intrinsic nature of desire and the other afflictions.
The Perfectly Awakened One seated in the vajra posture, who teaches the sublime Dharma of the ultimate meaning;
the treasury of omniscient wisdom, the Buddha Padmasambhava,
the sovereign amidst a multitude of emanations, the Great Vidyādhara and Honored Buddha.
The great adamantine sharp sword that severs all suffering and affliction,
the most supreme and pure syllable, the adamantine great vessel of the Dharma,
the adamantine profound meaning— this is realized by adamantine wisdom.
Possessing all the pāramitās, he is the adornment of the great earth;
through the purity of the selflessness of phenomena, he is the root of correct wisdom and the mind that is a net of illusory transformations—
the Great Teaching, the Lord of all teachings.
Supreme Vajra-born, supreme mass of great wisdom,
the wondrous mind of Samantabhadra; Lord of the World, Kṣitigarbha,
the great Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas, who manifests the wheel of manifold transformations.
The supreme self-nature of all natures; the meaning of the various phenomena of the unborn nature of the mind;
through the self-nature of all dharmas, O Mahāmati, in a single instant, one realizes all dharmas.
The Samādhi Manifesting All Dharmas, The true and great silence that realizes all Buddhas—
The Honored One, the Perfectly Enlightened One,
emits the light of great wisdom, Illuminating the selfless nature of all things.

The First Fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-mañjuśrī-mūla-jñāna-parama-rahasya-sarvārtha-nāma-samādhi* The Second Fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-mañjuśrī-mūla-jñāna-parama-rahasya-sarvārtha-nāma-samādhi*
Translated from the Sanskrit by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial:
This Ritual for the Accomplishment of Viśva-siddhi.
It is capable of manifesting various bodies through supreme transformations and purifying all evil realms.
Acting as the sovereign and the refuge for all sentient beings,
may you cause the entire realm of sentient beings to attain universal liberation;
entering the battle array of afflictions, may you be courageous and steadfast.
The great enemy of ignorance has been utterly destroyed without remainder;
with courageous hearts that never retreat, they possess majestic and supreme auspiciousness.
Manifesting fearless forms and marks, all beings are humbled and brought into submission.
Sometimes he manifests a body of majestic power, with a hundred arms and a countenance of fierce wrath;
or again, he performs the gesture of planting his feet, pressing down upon the earth while manifesting a dancing posture;
or he displays the Auspicious Arm, dwelling freely in the midst of space.
Either with one foot touching the ground, he forms a great maṇḍala;
or extending a single toe, he transcends the realm of Brahmā.
One should understand that all these transformations are but a single dharma, without duality.
Mastery over all phenomena, the most supreme ultimate truth,
and the various forms of manifest color and so forth— all these are produced by spiritual power.
All mental consciousnesses and dharmas arise from skillful means.
All past defilements have been purified, forming the three distinct realms of existence;
that supreme emptiness above all is truly unmoving.
Like the first appearance of the autumn moon, the dark clouds are entirely cleared away.
The Maṇḍala of the Dharmadhātu, which cannot be defiled by desire and the like,
is a supreme maṇi-jewel; manifesting as the colors of Indra’s blue and great blue,
it is the most excellent auspiciousness, adorned by the emanations of the Buddhas.
Manifesting the great strides of supernormal power, he causes the three realms to tremble everywhere;
possessing all samādhis, he maintains his own nature through right mindfulness,
and discriminates the four foundations of mindfulness and so forth according to reality.
The blossoming flowers of the seven factors of enlightenment, Their fragrance wafting throughout all realms;
Proclaiming the Eightfold Noble Path, Perfecting the fruits of all wisdom.
The ocean of the Tathāgata’s virtues, From which all phenomena arise.
May all sentient beings universally attain the path of perfect enlightenment;
May the minds of all classes of beings be unattached like space,
And may the intentions of sentient beings be swift and agile.
The faculties, desires, and natures of sentient beings— all their various distinctions—
are understood through the true meaning of the five aggregates;
one perceives the purity of the five aggregates as all that is produced by transformation, and all matters of those who are transformed.
Everything spoken by emanations abides in the reality-limit;
those twelve links of existence are the purity of the twelve aspects.
The characteristics of the teaching on the Four Noble Truths are fully realized through the eight knowledges.
The true meaning of the twelve marks, the reality of the sixteen marks,
and the twenty characteristics of perfect enlightenment—
these various characteristics of all phenomena are all taught by the Buddha as his emanations.
Manifesting all emanation bodies, causing all to observe in a single instant;
manifesting all samādhis in a single instant, comprehending all mental phenomena.
Proclaiming the skillful means of the various vehicles, Universally benefiting all worlds;
Although the three vehicles are clearly taught, One abides in the holy fruit of the Single Vehicle.
When the realm of afflictions is purified, The realms of karma are then exhausted.
Having crossed the ocean of afflictions, Abiding in the correspondence of all phenomena with afflictions and secondary afflictions, He brings them to cessation without remainder;
Arising through the skillful means of compassion and wisdom, He benefits himself and the world.
If all perceptions are severed, then all mental phenomena are extinguished;
the sphere of activity of the mind ceases, and having transcended the sphere of activity of the mind,
the mind dwells in peace, with all mental factors in equilibrium.
Born from the joyful minds of sentient beings, you are the accomplishment of great bliss for the minds of all beings, the most supreme cloud.
You are the Great Awakened Honored One of the three times who can dispel the darkness of all clouds; you are the great mass of merit.
The meaning of the five aggregates across the three times— observing them exhaustively in each moment,
one can realize them in each moment. The self-nature of all Buddhas,
the unattached supreme body— this is the true reality of the body.
Manifesting all manner of forms, the Great Maṇi Jewel Banner,
the Buddhas, the Truly Awakened Ones, proclaim the unsurpassed Great Bodhi through the three great mantras,
which are free from the conceptualization of words and letters.
The ultimate meaning of all vidyā-mantras is devoid of characteristics such as letters;
it is the great emptiness of the five syllables, and even the characteristics of the hundred syllables are empty.
All characteristics are non-characteristics, including the sixteen characteristics and so forth.
Signless and unmoving, dwelling with a mind established in the four dhyānas,
possessing all factors of concentration, encompassed by samādhi,
supreme in body through samādhi, and having mastery over all bodies.
The supreme body of the emanation, manifested by all Buddhas,
transforms all directions through its own power; according to principle, it delivers the world,
including all the lords of the devas, the celestial assistants, and the hosts of devas.
As well as the Amara devas, and even the asuras—
thus all such devas were each tamed by the Buddha’s supernormal transformations,
as he dwelt in the samādhis of all buddhas.
In the worlds of the ten directions, there is one supreme guide who acts as a great donor of the Dharma;
with the two dharmas of compassion and loving-kindness, he donning the firm armor to extensively deliver all beings from the ocean of existence.
Wielding the sword of wisdom and so forth, he destroys the four kinds of Māras who are great enemies of the afflictions, as well as all their demonic retinues;
he completely subdues those who ruin the wholesome Dharma and are difficult to tame, through perfect awakening.
Once the celestial Māras have taken refuge in the Buddha,
they completely abandon their minds of pride and offer respectful worship. To the Tathāgata,
the most supreme teacher within the three realms, he extends his great strides through divine power.
He reveals the Dharma of the three knowledges (*traividya*), the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*),
and the six recollections (*ṣaḍanusmṛti*). To the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas,
he has fully perfected the power of past lives and the ultimate *pāramitā* of true, supreme wisdom.
The Sovereign of all selves, the supreme *pudgala* beyond all analogy,
the donor of the unsurpassed gift of Dharma whom wisdom cannot fathom—
he has proclaimed the meaning of the four seals.
For the benefit of the world, he has brought forth the supreme ultimate truth of the three vehicles;
he is the most excellent lord of the three times,
auspicious in all his deeds, the sublime root of wondrous virtue.
I take refuge in the Great Vow of the Vajra; I take refuge in the principle of the reality-limit of *tathatā*;
I take refuge in the sublime treasury of emptiness; I take refuge in the unsurpassed Buddha-bodhi;
I take refuge in the Dharma beloved by the Buddhas; I prostrate and take refuge in the wisdom-body of the Buddha.
I take refuge in the Buddhas, the Kings of Great Joy; I prostrate and take refuge in the Buddhas, the Great Delights.
I take refuge in the Buddhas, the Dharmas of Right Mindfulness; I prostrate and take refuge in the Buddhas, the Great Laughs.
I take refuge in the Buddhas, the Right Speech taught by the Buddha; I prostrate and take refuge in the Buddhas, the Self-Nature.
Homage to the one who does not follow any state of existence; Homage to the one born from perfect wisdom;
Homage to the one born from the nature of space; Homage to the one who gives birth to all-knowledge;
Homage to the supreme net of illusory manifestations; Homage to the great play of all Buddhas.
Praised by all sentient beings, I therefore take refuge in the mass of perfect wisdom.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Great Vajradhara,
regarding the secret names and meanings as I have explained them:
This is the crown of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas,
the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas,
produced from the fundamental, authentic wisdom of Mañjuśrī.
The most supreme, uncommon, and pure perfection of the merits of all Buddhas;
the Dharma of the highest praise and great joy;
the vast, divine power, majesty, and ultimate truth.
The secret purity of the actions of body, speech,
and mind is such that the merits of the various pāramitās and stages (bhūmis) are pure,
perfect, and without any diminution or loss.
All those phenomena produced by merit and wisdom are perfectly pure;
this is called the supreme, incomparable ultimate truth (*paramārtha*).
By means of these phenomena, all who have not yet attained the fruit shall cause them to be attained.
This is the supreme dhāraṇī of the ultimate meaning, the unsurpassed Dharma-eye of all Tathāgatas.
It is to be understood as it truly is and proclaimed according to the principle.
Vajrapāṇi, you should now know this secret name and its meaning.
Sustained by the majestic power of all Buddhas,
this is the meaning of the supreme great illusory transformation;
among all dhāraṇī methods, it is the Great Invincible One.
The supreme white dharma is perfectly pure,
extending even to the reality of the secrets of body, speech, and mind of the knowledge of all-knowing wisdom;
it is able to realize the samādhi of the manifest presence of the perfect enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.
They skillfully enter the unsurpassed dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas;
they cannot be defeated by any demonic powers;
and they accomplish the meritorious qualities of the ten powers of a Tathāgata.
It transcends all the ten powers of the bodhisattvas;
it accomplishes the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna) and transcends all other forms of knowledge; it is the ultimate refuge of all dharmas;
and it universally gathers the stainless purity of all the Buddha-teachings.
Born from merit and wisdom, it is vast and perfect;
with the great bodhisattvas as its retinue,
it increases and blazes forth, even while abiding within all the realms of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, humans, and devas.
In accordance with those dharmas, they constantly abide in the supreme Mahāyāna;
they give rise to the boundless and excellent practices of a bodhisattva,
and ultimately penetrate all the dharmas of the noble paths.
Having attained liberation for themselves,
they are further able to manifest transformations and all modes of practice, ensuring that the lineage of the Buddhas is never interrupted;
endowed with great wisdom, they abide within the clan of Bodhisattvas.
He embraces all supreme verbal actions,
destroys all the teachings of external paths,
acts as a valiant army to subdue the four māras, and attains invincibility.
Furthermore, they are able to universally gather all sentient beings,
reveal the noble path, and give rise to all dharmas;
they abide eternally in samādhi and practice the four brahma-vihāras.
While abiding in one-pointed concentration through dhyāna,
having perfected the yogic actions of body, speech, and mind,
he attains the total exhaustion of all afflictions and secondary afflictions.
One is then able to sever all fetters and bonds;
liberated by great wisdom,
one brings all minds to tranquility.
It stills all hindrances,
extinguishes all views,
and remains far removed from all signs.
They are able to close all doors to unwholesome rebirths;
they are fully liberated within the path of the true truths, crushing the wheel of birth and death,
turning the great Dharma wheel, and establishing the great Dharma banner.
Abiding securely in the vast Dharma teachings of the Tathāgata,
he proclaims all dharmas in accordance with the capacities and needs of sentient beings,
swiftly accomplishing the gateway of secret practices.
Observing the intrinsic nature of all bodhisattvas,
they fulfill the gateway of the perfection of wisdom and awaken to the emptiness of all bodhisattvas.
Realizing the liberation of all non-duality;
giving birth to all dharmas of the pāramitās;
and penetrating all dharmas of the pāramitās.
It brings to full perfection and purification all stages [of the path].
This secret name and meaning comprehensively encompasses the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths of the Śrāvakas,
as well as the Dharmas from the four applications of mindfulness up to the eightfold noble path.
Thus, although these phenomena are differentiated,
one awakens to them with a single mind as non-dual;
this is called the perfection of the merits of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, the Great Vajradhara:
this secret name and meaning is the practice gate for the accomplishment of the supreme physical, verbal, and mental actions of all sentient beings.
It pacifies and eliminates all sinful dharmas of sentient beings,
purifies all evil destinies,
and severs all karmic obstructions.
One shall never again undergo rebirth in the eight difficult states;
the eight kinds of great fears shall be pacified and eliminated;
and all evil dreams and inauspicious omens shall be destroyed.
One does not give rise to thoughts of any unwholesome objects,
destroys all most evil realms,
and remains far removed from all demonic activities.
No improper mental attention arises even for a moment;
all views of self-attachment and the like are severed,
and no afflictions of sorrow or suffering arise.
It increases all roots of merit, wisdom, and goodness;
it abides securely in the reality of the heart-mind of all Tathāgatas and the secret reality of all Bodhisattvas.
The secret reality of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
the reality of all mudrās, signs, and vidyā-mantras;
and the conformity to all speech and action that is in accordance with reason, characterized by right mindfulness and right awareness.
Furthermore, this Dharma can, within the present life, increase wisdom,
eliminate all illnesses, and bring about the perfection of physical strength,
as well as wealth, happiness, and sovereignty.
Auspicious and pure, it increases wholesome dharmas;
one attains great renown and is praised in song, becoming beloved by all people.
This secret dharma brings about great benefit.
It pacifies all diseases and great terrors;
it causes all that is false and delusive to become true;
and it transforms all inauspicious signs into auspicious signs.
He causes all that is not supreme to become supreme, and all that is inauspicious to become auspicious.
He acts as the sovereign for those who have no master,
and serves as the refuge for those who have no support.
He acts as a protector for those who have no refuge;
he acts as a place of reliance for those who have nowhere to turn;
he acts as a lamp for those dwelling in darkness.
For those who have no destination, he reveals the true, correct path;
for those submerged in the ocean of birth and death, he acts as a boat and raft for their genuine deliverance;
and as a great king of physicians, he cures all manner of ailments.
Through the wisdom of reality, one realizes that the nature of things is both existent and non-existent;
this true worldly knowledge pierces through all the darkness and blindness of ignorance,
acting as a great sovereign wish-fulfilling jewel for all sentient beings according to their needs.
Whatever aspirations one may have shall all be fulfilled.
Furthermore, this secret dharma is the true body of wisdom of Mañjuśrī, the wisdom of omniscience;
it is the body of wisdom that appears as perfectly pure attainment.
The six pāramitās attained through the five eyes of reality;
the truly perfect and supreme gift of Dharma;
and the attainment of the dharmas of the ten stages, free from falsehood and fear.
Abiding in that which is born of true merit and wisdom,
he is fully endowed with the perfection of the factors of samādhi;
abiding in the single dharma, he is free from the characteristics of dual dharmas.
The reality-limit of true thusness is devoid of all forms and has no distinct dharmic nature.
One dwells well in dhyāna within the reality-limit of true thusness;
the characteristics of form are pure and free from all delusive marks.
The Tathāgata’s self-nature arises from perfect wisdom.
Since the nature of form within the great emptiness of all marks is free from attachment, how could there be any view?
When all marks are free from views, one attains all dharmas.
This is the true meaning of the secret name.
It refers to the ultimate truth (paramārtha) that arises from non-dual dharmatā;
all those who uphold and explain it are likewise so.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Great Vajradhara,

this is the section on the samādhi of the secret name and meaning, which is the fundamental wisdom of Mañjuśrī, the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas, the wisdom-peak, the absolute non-dual, supreme, and most excellent.
This is the adornment of the great maṇi-jewel crest;
among all teachings, there is no dharma that can surpass it.
If there are those who truly practice the mantra path, [they shall attain this].

Those who delight in practicing this gateway of secret mantra conduct should select an auspicious and excellent location and construct a maṇḍala according to their capacity and at an appropriate time.
Arrange an image of Vairocana Tathāgata and make offerings according to one's means.
With the highest single-mindedness, contemplate it with true reality;
focus your attention intently upon the consecrated sacred image, remaining free from all distraction.
Thereafter, with right speech and action, three times each day, one should receive,
uphold, recite, memorize, and contemplate the secret vidyā-mantra;
when reciting it, one should maintain this practice.
With speech and mind in accord, ensure that the words and phrases are complete, correct, and free from confusion; then,
with a mind of faith and understanding, apply authentic mental attention (*bhūtamanasikāra*) toward this gateway of secret mantra practice.
Having thus cultivated and attained proficiency,
one immediately obtains everything desired according to one's wishes and realizes the supreme ultimate truth of all phenomena.
Having realized unimpeded wisdom and being fully endowed with faith free from dualistic discrimination,
they are able to thoroughly know the events of the three periods of time.
Furthermore, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas appear before them.
He reveals the gateway for the arising of all phenomena,
thereby being able to illuminate and penetrate the intrinsic nature of self and dharmas.
Once the practitioner of yoga has thus achieved accomplishment,
He was immediately able to perform various transformations,
manifesting as the Great Wrathful King Vajrapāṇi,
who is capable of subduing all those who are difficult to tame.
They deliver the world and bring about great benefit;
manifesting various physical forms with great radiance,
they are further able to accomplish all things.
By means of the vidyā-mantra, mudrā, signs, samādhi,
and maṇḍala rites, one becomes the most supreme great vidyā-king of mantras.
All those who are extremely evil pināyakas [are subdued].
Even unto Māra and the hosts of Māra,
they shall constantly provide protection throughout the day and night;
remaining invisible in all places, they shall always follow after them.
They shall not allow any evil to find an opportunity to seize them;
furthermore, they shall receive the compassionate grace of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
establishing all their actions of body, speech, and mind so that they abide eternally in the True Dharma.
They are collectively sustained by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas;
they have attained fearless eloquence regarding all dharmas;
and they have thoroughly penetrated all the dharmas of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
And they are able to contemplate the selflessness of intrinsic nature. All Brahmā kings,
Śakras, Rudras, and Nārāyaṇas—
The youthful deity Maheśvara,
the deity Kārttikeya Mahākāla,
and the deity Nandikeśvara.
The Fire Devas, Water Devas, Wind Devas, Hārītī, and so forth,
up to the World-Protectors of the ten directions—
all such hosts of devas.
Throughout day and night, they shall also constantly provide protection,
ensuring that the yogin remains secure and at ease whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,
and always abides in samādhi, free from all distraction.
Whether dwelling alone in a single place, or entering among a great multitude of people,
or even entering royal cities, towns, villages, hamlets, alleys, empty houses, mountain forests, rivers, and so forth.
Whether they are staying or rising, at all times and in all their activities,
those devas will constantly provide secret protection.
Furthermore, whether they remain in their own homes or dwell elsewhere, day and night, [they shall be protected].
Furthermore, there were devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth,
as well as the various lunar mansions and planets, along with hosts of spirits.
These are the so-called assemblies of the Noble Radiant Mothers (*ārya-jyotirmātṛ*),
the seven mother goddesses (*sapta-mātṛkā*), and even the assemblies of the Yakṣiṇīs,
Rākṣasīs, and Piśācīs, and suchlike groups.
Each of them, together with their respective retinues, shall constantly come to provide protection,
so that those practitioners who cultivate yoga may attain a most excellent physical form, strength, and firmness, free from all diseases.
One's lifespan will increase and one shall obtain great auspiciousness.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Great Vajradhara,
if there be any practitioners who cultivate yoga:
Regarding this *Sarvaguhyārthanāmasamādhibhāga-mahāmaṇicūḍa*, one should diligently practice by focusing the mind upon it,
reciting it, and maintaining mindfulness three times each day.
Furthermore, one should dwell the mind in the visualization of the sacred image of the deity.
From the sublime wisdom of Mañjuśrī, emanation bodies arise,
manifesting in infinite varieties of forms and colors.
Having observed in this way,
before long the very forms and characteristics being contemplated will appear;
furthermore, one will immediately see all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
In the midst of space, there appeared countless bodies of various colors;
furthermore, this was due to the merit of these most excellent dharmas of the practitioner who cultivates yoga.
They shall never again fall into any of the evil destinies;
in future lives, they shall not be born into lowly lineages,
nor in border regions, nor shall they possess inferior faculties.
They are not born together with those whose faculties are incomplete;
furthermore, they are not born into families of wrong views,
nor do they take birth in lands that are not Buddha-fields.
The Buddha does not appear in the world to proclaim the True Dharma, nor does he undergo birth;
he never takes birth among the long-lived devas,
and he never takes birth in the evil world of the five turbidities.
They shall not be born during the kalpas of famine or the kalpa of weapons.
In every lifetime, they shall remain far removed from the terrors of enemies, adversaries, thieves, and robbers.
In whatever place they are born, they shall not undergo the suffering of poverty.
He cannot be moved by fame or praise;
in every lifetime he is born into a noble family;
and his physical marks are fully endowed, upright and perfect.
Within the world, they will be loved and respected by people;
they will constantly experience happiness and be free from all sorrow and affliction.
In whatever place they are born, all people will rejoice at the sight of them.
Their speech shall be truthful and sincere, such that others will trust and accept it;
in life after life and birth after birth, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives;
they shall possess great wealth and have a large retinue.
They increase the inexhaustible, supreme merits of all sentient beings, fully possessing them all;
they likewise fully possess the inherent merits of the six pāramitās.
They have fully perfected the four brahma-vihāras;
they are endowed with right mindfulness, right awareness, skillful means, and the power of aspiration;
and they have thoroughly mastered all pure teachings.
Through mastery over verbal karma, one attains great fearlessness;
in all debates and discussions, one’s eloquence is unimpeded,
and one is further able to comfort all sentient beings.
They were no different from his ācārya and preceptors;
even those categories of all dharmas never heard before,
up to and including all worldly literary treatises.
He has attained complete mastery of external treatises and the like,
and has acquired great eloquence, the perfection of ethical discipline, and a long life—
all pure and fully accomplished.
They always delight in leaving the household life and are fully endowed with the various precepts;
they never forget or lose the mind of omniscience,
and their great bodhicitta is firm and indestructible.
They transcend the realm of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
nor do they take delight in their respective dharmas.
O Vajrapāṇi, all you practitioners of yoga!
One shall obtain such immeasurable merits, fully endowed with them all,
and swiftly accomplish the fruit of great enlightenment (*mahābodhi*).
Furthermore, this secret name and its meaning possess immeasurable and boundless portions of great merit, which are perfectly complete and fulfilled.
Even if one were to praise and extol it for immeasurable eons, one could never reach its end.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Great Vajradhara,
the Tathāgatas appear in the world through the skillful means of great compassion.
Having attained perfection in the meaning of these secret names,
one achieves *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* born of merit and wisdom,
universally gathering all the jewel-like virtues of the Buddhas.
There is not the slightest dharma that is not perfected;
for the sake of all sentient beings,
he beats the great Dharma drum throughout the lands of the ten directions.
May all beings be established securely in the unsurpassed True Dharma,
the king of all dharmas taught by the Buddhas.
That is to say, this great vidyā-mantra is as follows:

Oṃ sarvadharmābhāvasvabhāvaviśuddhe dharmatājuḥ ā āṃ aḥ. All phenomena are pure by their own nature; they are neither born nor extinguished. They arise from the wisdom-body of all Tathāgatas, Mañjuśrī, the purity of the fundamental source.
That is to say:
ĀḤ, the fundamental heart-mantra of all Tathāgatas.
That is to say:

Hara hara oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ! At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, having heard the Buddha preach this secret dharma,
rose from his seat with palms joined in joy. He prostrated before the Honored One Śākyamuni and the assembly of Buddhas,
sages, and holy ones, as well as the Supreme Lord of the Secret Vajra.
Having extended universal homage to all the wrathful vidyārājas, he spoke these words:

"Excellent, excellent! O Sovereign of Supreme Joy, you have well explained how to accomplish the fruit of perfect enlightenment for the benefit of myself and all sentient beings through your compassion."
The Buddha is the Great Guide of the world, leading all to return to the gateway of liberation;
he proclaims the most supreme and pure path, the King of Tantras of Secret Yoga.
This most excellent, vast, and profound meaning brings benefit to the entire world.
This is the sacred realm of all Buddhas, proclaimed by all Tathāgatas.
This concludes the lower fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-paramaśrīmañjuśrīmūlaprajñā-paramarahasya-sarvārtha-nāmasamādhi*.
